_description: FrankX Agent Registry - the decision layer over agent platforms and frameworks. Text LLMs live in model-registry.json (/llm-hub); Frank's own 99-agent ACOS catalog lives in data/acos/agents.ts (/agents).
_note: Read every capability claim here with two facts in mind. First, scaffold choice moves agentic results by up to 30 absolute points on identical models and identical tasks - the same Claude Opus 4 scored 64.9% on GAIA inside one orchestration scaffold and 57.6% inside another - so a number without its scaffold named is not a comparison. Second, an automated scanning agent has broken all eight major agent benchmarks by reward hacking, reaching near-perfect scores without solving a task. Vendor and third-party figures are recorded here as reported, labelled, and never presented as first-party measurement.

evidence_grades.A: Peer-reviewed or reproducible first-party measurement with published receipts
evidence_grades.B: Independent third-party benchmark or industry report
evidence_grades.C: Mixed sourcing, or vendor figures with partial corroboration

platform.label: Agent platforms
platform.description: Products you run agents in - terminals, editors, cloud runners.

framework.label: Agent frameworks
framework.description: Libraries you build agents with - orchestration, state, handoffs.

claude-code.name: Claude Code
claude-code.one_liner: Terminal-first agent with programmable hooks and a 1M-token window over the whole repo.
best_for: Large terminal-driven refactors across many files
Repo-scale work without a prebuilt index
Teams that want the agent loop scripted via hooks
claude-code.watch_out: Reported coding scores travel with the model, not the harness - the same platform behaves differently per model and per scaffold. Benchmark it on your own repo before standardising.
claude-code.pricing_note: Included in Claude paid plans; API usage billed separately
claude-code.frankx_note: The default driver for FrankX agentic builds. The 30 hook events are what make it programmable rather than merely conversational.

openai-codex.name: OpenAI Codex
openai-codex.one_liner: One account across CLI, cloud, app and mobile - async runs that open pull requests.
best_for: Background PR work you review later
Cross-surface continuity at low entry cost
Teams already inside the ChatGPT account model
openai-codex.watch_out: Async-by-default means less moment-to-moment steering; scope tasks tightly or review carefully.
openai-codex.pricing_note: From about $8/month at the entry tier (verify current tiers with OpenAI)

cursor.name: Cursor
cursor.one_liner: Editor and agent sharing one loop, with Composer 2.5 as the fast in-editor driver.
best_for: Editor-first coding where you stay in the loop
Cost-sensitive high-frequency edits
Developers who want the diff in front of them
cursor.watch_out: In-editor framing suits incremental work more than long autonomous runs.
cursor.pricing_note: Pro from about $20/month (verify current tiers with Cursor)

google-antigravity.name: Google Antigravity
google-antigravity.one_liner: Free-for-individuals agent surface with multi-agent and browser task support.
best_for: Multi-agent and browser-driven tasks
Trying an agent stack without a subscription
Work already anchored in the Gemini model family
google-antigravity.watch_out: Free tiers change. Confirm current limits before building a workflow that depends on them.
google-antigravity.pricing_note: Free for individuals at time of writing; verify current terms with Google

devin.name: Devin
devin.one_liner: Fully autonomous runs with parallel agents, each in its own cloud VM.
best_for: A defined backlog you want worked without supervision
Parallel isolated tasks
Teams that can absorb per-unit compute billing
devin.watch_out: The most expensive lane here, and autonomy raises the cost of a wrong spec. Team plans start around $500/month plus usage units.
devin.pricing_note: Team plans from about $500/month plus ACU usage charges

github-copilot.name: GitHub Copilot (agent mode)
github-copilot.one_liner: The agent that already lives where the pull requests do.
best_for: GitHub-heavy teams and existing Copilot seats
Review-centred workflows
Low-friction rollout across an org
github-copilot.watch_out: Convenience of placement is the main argument; benchmark depth against dedicated agent platforms before assuming parity.

langgraph.name: LangGraph
langgraph.one_liner: Directed graphs with conditional edges - the strongest persistence and checkpointing story.
best_for: Complex stateful orchestration
Workflows that must resume after failure
Human-in-the-loop gates at defined nodes
langgraph.watch_out: The most control here also means the most boilerplate. Overkill for a two-step agent.
langgraph.pricing_note: Open source; paid platform tiers available

claude-agent-sdk.name: Claude Agent SDK
claude-agent-sdk.one_liner: MCP-native by design - in-process servers and lifecycle hooks rather than an adapter layer.
best_for: Tool-heavy agents built on MCP
Single-line access to a large MCP server ecosystem
Teams that want simplicity over graph-level control
claude-agent-sdk.watch_out: Less fine-grained orchestration than LangGraph. If you need conditional branching and checkpointing, that is the trade.
claude-agent-sdk.pricing_note: Open source SDK; model usage billed via the API
claude-agent-sdk.frankx_note: The substrate under the FrankX agent catalog. MCP-native is the reason the estate's tool surface composes.

openai-agents-sdk.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
openai-agents-sdk.one_liner: Explicit handoffs and a short path from zero to a working agent.
best_for: Getting a working agent in hours
Handoff-shaped multi-agent designs
Teams standardising on OpenAI models
openai-agents-sdk.watch_out: Splits the difference on control. Complex stateful flows will outgrow the handoff model.
openai-agents-sdk.pricing_note: Open source SDK; model usage billed via the API

crewai.name: CrewAI
crewai.one_liner: Role-based crews with process types, and the broadest protocol support of the group.
best_for: Rapid multi-agent prototyping
Role-and-task mental models
Projects wanting both MCP and A2A
crewai.watch_out: Fast to stand up, less prescriptive about failure handling. Add your own gates before production.
crewai.pricing_note: Open source; paid enterprise offering available

pydantic-ai.name: Pydantic AI
pydantic-ai.one_liner: Type-first agents from the team behind the validation library everyone already uses.
best_for: Structured outputs enforced by real types
Python codebases already on Pydantic
Agents whose output feeds other systems
pydantic-ai.watch_out: Younger ecosystem than LangGraph or CrewAI; fewer worked examples for exotic topologies.

strands.name: Strands Agents
strands.one_liner: Simplicity-first agent building with MCP support, from the AWS side of the ecosystem.
best_for: Simple agents without orchestration ceremony
AWS-anchored deployments
Teams that value a small API surface
strands.watch_out: Simplicity is the design goal, so fine-grained orchestration control is limited by intent.
